questionText: How do you validate JSON request bodies in Spring Boot?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can implement nested request-body validation in Spring MVC and place conversion, DTO, domain, authorization, and database checks at the correct boundaries.
inScope: Jakarta Validation constraints on request DTOs
Cascaded validation for nested collection elements
Stable client-facing validation errors and focused tests
prerequisites: Java records or simple DTO classes

claims.statement: Spring MVC first uses HTTP message conversion to create the declared @RequestBody object; malformed JSON or incompatible target values fail before Bean Validation can inspect that object.

Applying @Valid to an @RequestBody parameter triggers Bean Validation for the converted request object, and normal Spring MVC handling treats a resulting MethodArgumentNotValidException as a 400 response.
Valid marks an association for cascaded validation, so List<@Valid OrderItemRequest> causes each contained item with constraints such as NotBlank and Positive to be validated.
Rules that depend on changing application state belong in service and authorization logic, while database constraints remain necessary to protect stored integrity when requests race.

examples.title: Compile the learner controller and verify invalid and valid nested item requests with MockMvc

validation.command: Run mvn -q test with Java 17 in an isolated Spring Boot 3.3.1 fixture using the exact request DTOs and controller plus a Jakarta Validation 3.0 validator
validation.expected: A nested item with quantity zero returns 400, while a valid nested item reaches the service and returns 201 with id 42

visuals.title: Request bytes moving through conversion, DTO constraints, domain checks, and persistence constraints

notes: The lesson clearly says that @Valid is a cascade marker rather than a constraint such as NotNull or Positive.
The integration check covers the exact nested-list case shown to learners instead of validating only a flat DTO.

review.notes: Spring MVC sequencing was checked against official Spring documentation, cascade and constraint behavior against Jakarta Validation 3.0, and the persistence boundary against Jakarta Persistence 3.1. The Java 17 Spring Boot 3.3.1 MockMvc fixture passed both invalid and valid paths.
